title.value: Parametric models for combined failure time data from an incident cohort study and a prevalent cohort study with follow-up
title.justification: The title accurately summarizes the content of the paper, which focuses on developing and analyzing parametric models for survival analysis using data from both incident and prevalent cohort studies.
title.quote: Parametric models for combined failure time data from an incident cohort study and a prevalent cohort study with follow-up

analysis.description: The paper addresses the problem of estimating failure time distributions by combining data from incident and prevalent cohort studies. It develops parametric models to improve statistical inference and examines the appropriateness of these models through theory and simulation. The application is demonstrated through the estimation of hospital stay durations.

type.justification: The paper develops and analyzes parametric models theoretically and supports the theory with simulation studies, rather than focusing on empirical data analysis.
type.quote: The theory we develop to address these questions is based on a parametrically defined failure time distribution and is supported by simulations.

name.justification: The primary research field of the paper is centered on survival analysis, specifically the estimation of failure time distributions using parametric models and right-censored data.

name.justification: The paper focuses on statistical methods applicable to biostatistics, specifically in the context of cohort studies and survival analysis.
name.quote: A classical problem in survival analysis is to estimate the failure time distribution from right-censored observations obtained from an incident cohort study.

name.justification: The paper applies its methodologies in the context of medical studies and hospital duration estimates, which are relevant to epidemiology.
